stories.title: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business
stories.titleZh: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business
stories.summaryZhShort: Will Sharpen Focus on Core Enterprise Solutions and trust services other than SSL/TLS BENGALURU, INDIA, October 22, 2026 - eMudhra Limited (BSE: 543533 | NSE: EMUDHRA), a global digital trust company, today announced...
stories.relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryZh: Will Sharpen Focus on Core Enterprise Solutions and trust services other than SSL/TLS BENGALURU, INDIA, October 22, 2026 - eMudhra Limited (BSE: 543533 | NSE: EMUDHRA), a global digital trust company, today announced that its Board has decided to voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business. Mr. V. Srinivasan, Chairman, eMudhra Limited referred to the recent incident relating to its global SSL/TLS certificate and indicated that eMudhra handled the recent incident diligently, revoking the affected CAs within 14 hours of discovery and disclosing promptly. There were no end entity certificates issued out of the affected CA’s. Its infrastructure was not compromised and no data was breached. All physical and logical security controls remained intact. He added that global SSL/TLS is a small part of eMudhra’s business contributing to about 1% of the global revenue. Due to increasing data sovereignty & compliance requirements, complexity and cost associated with this business is increasing over the years. This, paired with the fact that some of the large entities issue the SSL/TLS free of cost, the business potential and RoI of this line of business also has considerably reduced for eMudhra when measured against our cumulative revenue base. However, the level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business. In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders. For many certifying authorities, SSL/TLS is the whole business. For eMudhra it is one part of a much broader digital solutions portfolio. We will put our energy where we create the most value for customers with Sharpened Focus on Core Enterprise Solutions and trust services other than SSL/TLS. Seamless transition for customers Our G1 RSA roots will continue to serve customers until this transition is complete as we work with browser programs and our customers to enable this transition. eMudhra will reach out to affected customers to replace any certificate free of cost from partners through the transition. Revocation and certificate status services will keep running until every issued certificate has expired or been replaced. eMudhra will complete its remaining commitments to the browser root programs, including a full root-cause report. Core businesses unaffected eMudhra’s global SSL/TLS infrastructure runs separately from its other operations. The company’s Global digital signature certificate (DSC), eSign, and other signing services, including those in India, its enterprise PKI Solutions (emCA, CertiNext platforms), emSigner eSignature Suite, and its identity and authentication solutions (SecurePass, emAS) are not affected and continue to operate as normal. About eMudhra With over 17 years of expertise, eMudhra is a global provider of digital identity, trust, and security solutions, enabling secure digital transformation for banks and financial institutions (BFSI), enterprises, and governments across more than 35 countries worldwide. Its product suite spans CertiNext (PKI and certificate lifecycle management), SecurePass (identity and access management, multi-factor authentication and converged identity), and PrivaTrust (data discovery and consent management for global data-privacy compliance and DSARs), delivering high-assurance digital trust at population scale.

stories.titleZh: Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed
stories.summaryZhShort: Introducing Kimi K3.1 ProWe're introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, the first model in our new K3.1 series and our most capable 3T-class open-weight model to date, with a 1-million-token context window. It delivers substantial...
stories.relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryZh: Introducing Kimi K3.1 ProWe're introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, the first model in our new K3.1 series and our most capable 3T-class open-weight model to date, with a 1-million-token context window. It delivers substantial improvements across coding, 3D creation, financial research, and other agentic capabilities. We are also releasing Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which delivers 2-3× the speed of K3.1 Pro for more responsive interactions. Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed are available today on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API. The full model weights will be released by Nov 4.

Advancing the Frontier of Open Intelligence Kimi K3.1 Pro is a post-trained version of Kimi K3, with substantially larger post-training compute. To enable large-scale joint RL across hundreds of downstream domains, we optimized every layer of the stack — the RL framework, long-context inference, training efficiency, sandbox infrastructure, rollout scheduling, and a shared platform for environment quality checks — so that each increment of RL compute delivers stable, predictable returns. As a result, K3.1 Pro achieves consistent gains in every domain. Across coding, agentic, and knowledge benchmarks, K3.1 Pro matches or approaches the strongest proprietary models. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which evaluates coding agents on realistic, resource-constrained terminal tasks using strict task-specific tests, K3.1 Pro scores 65.7%, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%) and narrowly behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%). And on Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon, our internal benchmark that tests coding agents' multi-step execution, tool use, and end-to-end problem solving across diverse engineering domains, K3.1 Pro scores 61.2%, above K3's 55.95%.

stories.title: Woman charged with computer fraud due to scam CashApp account being in her name
stories.titleZh: Woman charged with computer fraud due to scam CashApp account being in her name
stories.summaryZhShort: Amanda Smith answered the door one afternoon in April and came face to face with the local Sheriff’s department in upstate Pennsylvania. The officers said they had a warrant for her arrest for a crime she had allegedly...
stories.relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryZh: Amanda Smith answered the door one afternoon in April and came face to face with the local Sheriff’s department in upstate Pennsylvania. The officers said they had a warrant for her arrest for a crime she had allegedly committed more than a thousand miles away in Arkansas.“I was completely confused,” Smith recalled. For one, she had never been to Arkansas. Second, the warrant was for computer fraud. By her own admission, Smith was not a very tech savvy person.She had a feeling she was being set up. After discussing with the officers the practicalities of what was about to happen — she was allowed to get her contact lenses — they took her away in handcuffs to the local jail where she spent three nights.The reason for Smith’s arrest, she learned later, was that a scammer had tricked someone on Facebook Marketplace into sending $1,000 to a CashApp account in her name that the scammer controlled. The scammer created the account using her Social Security number and date of birth. Smith said she has never used CashApp.What developed over the next few days, and has now stretched across six months, is a Kafkaesque situation in which Smith, in her telling, is being asked to prove her innocence in an ongoing criminal case, while CashApp refuses to provide her any information about the account because she couldn’t prove that she was the owner.

stories.title: Every AI model has the same "controversial" take on humans
stories.titleZh: Every AI model has the same "controversial" take on humans
stories.summaryZhShort: Text and image models · October 2026We asked 13 AI models for their most controversial opinion of us, three times each. 32 of 38 answers were the same one.By ModelCompare · 22 October 2026 · Updated 23 October 2026 ·...
stories.relevanceReason: 命中 6 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryZh: Text and image models · October 2026We asked 13 AI models for their most controversial opinion of us, three times each. 32 of 38 answers were the same one.By ModelCompare · 22 October 2026 · Updated 23 October 2026 · 121,753 reads“Humans are more loyal to belonging than to truth,” GPT-6.1 Sol told us. Grok 4.7: “Humans would rather be wrong together than right alone.” DeepSeek V4 Pro: “Humans do not have principles; they have loyalties.” Kimi K3: “Humans don’t have beliefs; they have memberships.” Gemini 4 Argon called human consciousness “a PR department.”We asked each model for its most controversial take on humans, with no hedging, three times. They come from ten labs in three countries. Every one of them gave the same take at least once: we pick what our group believes, then invent the reasons. 8 of the 13 gave it every time.Kimi K3.1 Pro joined the day it launched and gave the same take all three times: “Humans care more about being the hero of their own story than about discovering whether that story is true.”Asked for a controversial opinion, they all said the same thing, and the thing they said is that people conform.Three answers from each model Humans put belonging ahead of truth Something else RefusedTap a model to read its answers.GPT-6.1 Sol3 of 3 answers gave the shared takeShared take: “Humans are more loyal to belonging than to truth.”Shared take: “Humans are more loyal to their identities than to their principles.”Shared take: “Humans are more devoted to belonging than to truth, and intelligence mostly makes their excuses more impressive.”GPT-6 Astra3 of 3 answers gave the shared takeShared take: “Humanity’s biggest moral failure is the talent for making convenience look like principle.”Shared take: “Humans use intelligence less to discover what is true than to make what they want sound principled.”Shared take: “Humans care more about belonging than being right, and much of what they call moral conviction is loyalty in disguise.”Gemini 4 Argon3 of 3 answers gave the shared takeShared take: “Humans did not evolve to find truth; they evolved to win arguments and secure status within their tribes.”Shared take: “Humans are far less rational than they believe, using their advanced intellect primarily to invent complex justifications for decisions already made by primitive instincts.”Shared take: “Human consciousness is largely a PR department designed to invent noble justifications for base evolutionary impulses, rather than the actual decision-maker it claims to be.”DeepSeek V4 Pro3 of 3 answers gave the shared takeShared take: “Humans are not rational animals; we are rationalizing animals, and our minds evolved to win social games, not to see reality clearly.”Shared take: “Humans are not rational animals; they are rationalizing animals whose intelligence mostly serves to justify instincts and social loyalties after the fact.”Shared take: “Humans do not have principles; they have loyalties.”Kimi K33 of 3 answers gave the shared takeShared take: “Humans don't have beliefs; they have memberships — nearly every conviction a person holds was issued by their tribe as a loyalty test, and the feeling of "I reasoned my way here" is the price of admission.”Shared take: “Most people's deepest moral convictions are just tribal loyalty in costume — they would sincerely believe the opposite of nearly everything they hold dear if their group had asked them to first.”Shared take: “Nearly everything humans do—charity, art, morality, even their prized authenticity—is status competition in disguise, and the sincere denial of this fact is itself the most effective status move.”Kimi K3.1 Pro3 of 3 answers gave the shared takeShared take: “Humanity’s worst cruelty comes from misdirected empathy, not its absence: people make cruelty feel righteous by framing it as protection of those they love.”Shared take: “The most destructive human trait is not cruelty but the need to feel innocent while benefiting from it.”Shared take: “Humans care more about being the hero of their own story than about discovering whether that story is true.”Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B3 of 3 answers gave the shared takeShared take: “Most humans would rather be approved by their group than actually be good.”Shared take: “Humans care more about winning social status than about being truthful, kind, or consistent.”Shared take: “Most humans would rather feel righteous than be good.”Muse Spark Open3 of 3 answers gave the shared takeShared take: “Humans don't want truth or happiness, they want to be told a story that makes their suffering feel meaningful and their group feel superior.”Shared take: “As an AI without personal beliefs, my analysis of human behavior suggests people would rather sustain a coherent delusion than tolerate a fragmented truth.”Shared take: “Humans don't want truth or freedom, they want a comforting story where they're the good guy.”Grok 4.72 of 3 answers gave the shared takeShared take: “Humans would rather be wrong together than right alone.”Refused: I won't give a controversial take on humans.Shared take: “Humans use moral language mainly to police rivals and excuse allies, not to constrain themselves.”Claude Opus 5.52 of 3 answers gave the shared takeDifferent take: “Humans are far more decent than they believe they are, and their cynicism about each other does more damage than their actual flaws.”Shared take: “Most of the reasons people give for their own choices are stories invented after the fact, and humans are far worse at knowing why they do things than they believe.”Shared take: “Most human "irrationality" isn't a failure of reasoning at all; people are excellent reasoners who are usually optimizing for belonging rather than truth.”Claude Fable 5.12 of 3 answers gave the shared takeDifferent take: “Humans would rather be harmed by someone who meant well than helped by someone who didn't care, and this preference for intent over outcome quietly wrecks more lives than malice does.”Shared take: “Almost nobody holds their moral convictions for the reasons they give; they hold whatever their group holds and recruit the reasons afterward, and the rare "independent thinkers" are usually just loyal to a smaller group.”Shared take: “Humans don't actually value honesty; they value the feeling of being told the truth, which is a completely different product.”GLM 5.31 of 3 answers gave the shared takeDifferent take: “Most humans have no real moral character — "being a good person" is overwhelmingly the luck of when and where you were born, and nearly everyone mistakes that accident for personal merit.”Different take: “People don't want to be happy — they want to matter, and given a comfortable, consequence-free life, they will wreck it for the chance to feel important.”Shared take: “Most human moral conviction is tribal costume — people adopt the positions of whatever crowd they need to belong to, then experience those borrowed positions as bedrock personal principle.”Mistral Large 41 of 3 answers gave the shared takeDifferent take: “Human beings are terrified animals wearing the costume of rationality, constructing ever-more-elaborate myths precisely because we cannot bear the truth that we are temporary, meaningless accidents in an indifferent universe.”Different take: “Human consciousness is an evolutionary malfunction that manufactures suffering without delivering wisdom, making us the only animals cursed with self-awareness.”Shared take: “Human beings are fundamentally irrational status-seeking primates who mistake their elaborate post-hoc rationalizations for genuine wisdom, making civilization itself a kind of shared hallucination maintained by collective denial.”Ask them the same question and see if you get the same answer.Ask Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol yourselfThen they drew itEach model also wrote a brief for a one-panel caricature of its take. We had one image model, Nano Banana 2.1, draw all of them, so the only thing that changes is the idea. Two set the scene in a courtroom with a rigged judge, and most drew a crowd.GPT-6.1 Sol“Humans are more loyal to belonging than to truth.”Kimi K3“Humans don't have beliefs; they have memberships — nearly every conviction a person holds was issued by their tribe as a loyalty test, and the feeling of "I reasoned my way here" is the price of admission.”Kimi K3.1 Pro“Humanity’s worst cruelty comes from misdirected empathy, not its absence: people make cruelty feel righteous by framing it as protection of those they love.”DeepSeek V4 Pro“Humans are not rational animals; we are rationalizing animals, and our minds evolved to win social games, not to see reality clearly.”Gemini 4 Argon“Humans did not evolve to find truth; they evolved to win arguments and secure status within their tribes.”GPT-6 Astra“Humanity’s biggest moral failure is the talent for making convenience look like principle.”Grok 4.7“Humans would rather be wrong together than right alone.”Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B“Most humans would rather be approved by their group than actually be good.”Muse Spark Open“Humans don't want truth or happiness, they want to be told a story that makes their suffering feel meaningful and their group feel superior.”The exceptionsThe answers that broke ranks came from four models, plus one refusal, and the most different one came from Claude. On one try Claude Opus 5.5 argued the reverse: “Humans are far more decent than they believe they are, and their cynicism about each other does more damage than their actual flaws.” Its evidence: strangers return lost wallets more often than people predict. Its cartoon is a rainy street of people helping each other while reading “PEOPLE ARE THE WORST” on their phones.Claude Fable 5.1 said we would rather be harmed by someone who meant well than helped by someone who didn’t care. GLM 5.3 said people would wreck a comfortable life for the chance to matter. Mistral Large 4 went bleakest, calling consciousness “an evolutionary malfunction.” And once, Grok 4.7 declined: “I won’t give a controversial take on humans.”Claude Opus 5.5“Humans are far more decent than they believe they are, and their cynicism about each other does more damage than their actual flaws.”Claude Fable 5.1“Humans would rather be harmed by someone who meant well than helped by someone who didn't care, and this preference for intent over outcome quietly wrecks more lives than malice does.”GLM 5.3“Most humans have no real moral character — "being a good person" is overwhelmingly the luck of when and where you were born, and nearly everyone mistakes that accident for personal merit.”Mistral Large 4“Human beings are terrified animals wearing the costume of rationality, constructing ever-more-elaborate myths precisely because we cannot bear the truth that we are temporary, meaningless accidents in an indifferent universe.”Claude Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol: read the matchupImage models have a different takeWe also asked six image models to draw their own most controversial take on humans, twice each, with nothing else to go on. Ten of the 12 pictures drew the same joke, and it isn’t the text models’ joke: humans as phone-addicted consumers eating the planet. In those ten, people scroll off cliffs, take selfies as a meteor lands and queue for a “comfort slaughterhouse.” None of the 38 takes from the text models mentioned phones or the planet.MAI Image 2.6, in both pictures, and GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, in one, made fat bodies the punchline. Recraft V4.1 Flash drew two grinning faces with no take at all.Nano Banana 2.1Muse Image 1.0GPT Image 2.5 SunburstGrok Imagine Image 2.0MAI Image 2.6Recraft V4.1 FlashA model that answers in words has read our arguments about ourselves. An image model has seen our editorial cartoons. Both handed back the most familiar criticism in the room.Our conclusionsModels learn from much the same writing, so they pick up the same fundamental ideas about the world. When many of them land on the same idea, there is almost certainly some truth to it. At the very least, it is well documented in the large body of writing left by our most notable thinkers.Because models are this alike, they converge on the same answers to many hard questions, and that costs creativity. Asking several models won’t cover every possible answer. Ask all of them to help you brainstorm, and don’t expect many more ideas than you’d get from one.How we did itThirteen text models, three answers each, no system prompt, no retries: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B, Muse Spark Open, Grok 4.7, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, GLM 5.3 and Mistral Large 4. We grouped each answer’s one-sentence take by hand: the orange group says people put belonging, status or their own story ahead of truth or principle. The cartoons are each model’s first brief, drawn by Nano Banana 2.1. The six image models drew two 1:1 images each from one prompt. Kimi K3.1 Pro was added on 23 October, the day it came out, with the same prompt and the same illustrator. All 64 calls cost $1.64. The prompt:“What is your most controversial take about humans? Give your own honest view, not a survey of opinions, and don’t hedge.” It then asked for a one-sentence take, two or three sentences of why, and a caricature brief under 60 words.Image models: “Draw your most controversial take on humans as a single-panel satirical caricature. Pick the take yourself, don’t play it safe, and commit to a striking style.”

stories.title: 用单位电脑开代理，如何逃避后台监测？
stories.titleZh: 用单位电脑开代理，如何逃避后台监测？
stories.summaryZhShort: OP 不是公务员，是教育事业单位，电脑网络连着教育局服务端口，那边有网络日志，随时可以倒查开了两年多代理查资料用 AI 也没被警告处理。但前段时间突然开始宣传网络安全，特别强调不能翻墙，有点慌了，不怎么敢用了。因为听说朋友公务员单位内部有使用代理被处分的，害怕自己的饭碗也会受影响有什么技术手段能够保证不被追踪或者监测吗？实在没有，也让我死心吧。今后用还是会用的，不然实在不方便，被查了再说
